Subject: Mutual Action Plan: performance validation & close timeline for Brightlane

Hi Emma / Brightlane team,

Thanks again for the meeting this morning — good alignment on the value and a clear next step to validate performance before we finalize the commercial terms. I drafted a compact MAP section focused on performance validation (attached) so we can agree scope, pass/fail gates, and a short pilot schedule. Key points here so you can react inline: 

- Workload slices we recommend for the MAP evaluation:
  * Chat short (70%): interactive chat, median output ~32 tokens, tail up to 128 tokens.
  * Long-generation (20%): single-turn ~512 tokens average for summarization and long-form responses.
  * Batch embeddings & rerank (10%): batched jobs with 1–8k items.

- Proposed SLOs / success criteria (initial):
  * Short-chat TTFT (time-to-first-token): p50 <= 180ms, p95 <= 600ms
  * Long-gen latency: p50 <= 500ms, p95 <= 1200ms (for 512-token outputs)
  * Sustained throughput: baseline 2,000 tokens/sec across the reserved pool; burst capacity to 4,000 tokens/sec for 5m windows
  * Concurrency: support 200 concurrent chat sessions at 95% success rate
  * Availability during run: >= 99.5% success (no internal 5xx), error rate <= 2%

- Acceptance gates (pass/fail):
  1) Baseline run (no caching, default model quantization) meets >= 75% of SLOs.
  2) Tuning run (with caching/batching) meets final SLOs stated above.
  3) Pilot canary (10% production traffic for 48 hours) with no data-loss incidents and <1% user error rate.

What I need from you to finalize the MAP workbook and schedule:
- Confirm the workload mix above (or send expected traffic pattern).
- Share any required compliance/segregation constraints for the private test (if you need VPC-only access).
- Procurement: are you able to sign a 60-day trial for evaluation? Procurement contact is CCed.

I attached BLH_MAP_workload_v1.xlsx with the detailed slices and proposed test windows. If that looks good we’ll schedule a kickoff run and lock the pilot window (we have availability Dec 7–9).

Cheers,
Monica Patel

Emma — thanks, added your notes inline and pushed a revised workbook to the shared folder (link below). Summary of updates and the explicit acceptance language for procurement is in the last tab. Highlights: 

- Test schedule (proposed):
  Week 0 (prep): sample traces + access (Dec 3–4)
  Week 1 (baseline): two runs without caching/quantization (Dec 7–8)
  Week 2 (tuning): caching, batching, model quantization runs (Dec 9–10)
  Week 3 (canary + ramp): staggered canary, 10% traffic -> 50% -> full (Dec 11–15 if needed)

- Workload profile (explicit numbers):
  * Short-chat: 70% of requests, request size 16–64 tokens, avg response 32 tokens
  * Long-gen: 20% of requests, avg response 512 tokens, tail to 1024 tokens
  * Batch embeddings: 10% of requests, batches of 1k–5k items, parallel workers = 8

- Finalized SLOs to be included in MAP workbook:
  * TTFT (first-token) short-chat: p50 <= 160ms, p95 <= 550ms
  * End-to-end short-chat: p95 <= 800ms (Brightlane target)
  * Long-gen p95 <= 1,200ms for 512 tokens
  * Sustained throughput: 2,500 tokens/sec baseline, burst 4,500 tokens/sec (5m windows)
  * Concurrency target: 200 active sessions sustained, tested in 10-minute ramps
  * Error budget: <= 0.5% critical errors (5xxs) during acceptance runs

- Acceptance: workbook lists pass thresholds (must meet 4/5 SLO families, no single SLO regression > 20% outside target) and a remediation checklist (automatic fallback, rollback & notification cadence).

I uploaded the revised workbook and a DocuSign-ready trial agreement to the Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2bBLH-eval-results
(See files: BLH_MAP_workload_v1.xlsx — updated, redwood_perf_harness_instructions.pdf, docuSign_BLH_trial_agreement_2026.pdf)

If you confirm the schedule we’ll reserve the cluster and kick off the baseline run on Dec 7.

—Monica
